input: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling

output.company: Rippling (People Center, Inc. d/b/a Rippling), San Francisco, CA

business.claim: Sells cloud HR, onboarding, payroll, finance and IT software as a monthly subscription. Co-founded by Parker Conrad and Prasanna Sankar and headquartered in San Francisco. The page gives both 2016 and 2017 as the founding year.
Company says it offers 'over two dozen products across HR, IT, and Spend', including payroll, benefits, SSO/identity management, bill pay and corporate cards.

Puts payroll, devices, building access, benefits and company cards on one platform. Company says its HR, IT and finance apps were built in-house rather than acquired and share one data layer. Rippling AI launched earlier in 2026.

Launched Rippling Data Cloud (data movement, storage, transformation and visualization) on June 25, 2026. The base SKU, bundled with Rippling AI, is about $20/month, plus usage-based charges. Also launched Business Banking: a high-yield checking account and same-day payroll.
Geographies: offices on four continents (San Francisco, New York City, Austin, Seattle, Toronto, London, Dublin, Bengaluru, Singapore, Sydney). Integrates with 600+ apps (company claim).
Released its own MCP gateway product right after the Runlayer lawsuits were dropped in August 2026.

traction.claim: Company claim: ARR passed $1B in 2025. In April 2026 Parker Conrad said revenue was growing 78% year over year and that growth had accelerated 'every quarter, for three straight quarters'.

Third-party tracker (ARR Club) reports Rippling passing $1B ARR with 78% YoY growth, citing a post on Parker Conrad's X account. The page also shows +81% in its summary box, which conflicts with the 78%.
Customers: 20,000+ as of May 2025, per aggregator Sacra. I did not find this figure in a Rippling disclosure.
Company claim reported by TechCrunch: about 560 companies use Data Cloud, with new revenue from the product running at roughly $5M–$7M per month.
Named customers in company case studies: NinjaTech AI, Kleiner Perkins, The Channel Company, Dude Wipes, Chess.com, Ignite Reading, Clariti (company claim).
Ranked No. 11 on CNBC's 2026 Disruptor 50, up from No. 29 in 2025.

team.claim: Current leadership per the company: Parker Conrad (Co-Founder & CEO), Matt MacInnis (President & CPO), Albert Strasheim (CTO), Adam Swiecicki (CFO), Matt Plank (CRO), Martin White (General Counsel), Stephanie Ho (SVP Customer Experience), Sunil Raman (SVP Business & Product Ops), Bridget Abraham (Chief Compliance Officer).
Parker Conrad started Rippling after he left Zenefits.
Rep. Mike Lawler's letter notes that Conrad was forced out of Zenefits, which New York regulators fined $1.2M over labor-law violations.
CNBC lists co-founder Prasanna Sankar under leadership, but he is not on Rippling's current leadership page. I found no confirmed departure date.

funding.claim: March 2023: raised almost $500M in a round arranged by Greenoaks Capital after the Silicon Valley Bank collapse froze withdrawals.
April 2024: valued at $13.5B in a Series F led by Coatue.

Series G: $450M new financing at a $16.8B valuation, plus a tender offer to buy back up to $200M of equity from current and former employees. Investors named: Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator, with existing investors participating. The post names no lead.
Total funding about $1.85B after the Series G (Wikipedia). CNBC gives about $1.8B and lists the Series G as the latest round as of May 2026.
Last confirmed valuation is $16.8B (May 2025). For comparison, Deel was valued at $17.3B in October 2025 and Ramp at $44B.
Conrad on an IPO: 'We are not going public.'

financial_signals.claim: Sacra estimates of annualized revenue: ~$570M (May 2025), ~$850M (end of 2025), ~$1.0B (March 2026), with 78% YoY growth.
Wikipedia: annual revenue around $1B in July 2026. The company was unprofitable in 2024 with about $1B in cash.
Conrad says Rippling is about two years from cash-flow positive. R&D is 45–50% of revenue, compared with about 8–9% at Paylocity and Paycom.
Internal AI token spend was on track to reach 40% of the R&D headcount budget and was growing 80% month over month. After new controls it fell to about 15%.
Headcount trend per Wikipedia: about 2,800 (2024) to about 5,000 (2025). The company does not publish a current number.
Sacra reports a plan to grow India headcount from 1,000 to 2,000 over three years, and 100+ in-house recruiters.
Was 'hiring across all roles' at the time of the Series G (company claim).
Received $7M in New York State tax subsidies in 2024–2025 to expand its NYC offices, per Rep. Lawler's office.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Rippling sued Deel on March 17, 2025, alleging racketeering, trade-secret theft, tortious interference, unfair competition, and aiding and abetting breach of fiduciary duty. The case centres on an employee allegedly spying for Deel. Deel denies wrongdoing.

People Center Inc. v. Deel Inc. (N.D. Cal., Judge Charles Breyer): on about September 25, 2026 the court rejected Deel's bid to bar testimony from Keith O'Brien and declined to revisit its February 2026 ruling, so Rippling's RICO and trade-secret claims proceed. The court dismissed Deel's cybersquatting and trademark counterclaims, which concern deal.com. Some of Deel's 32 Lanham Act false-advertising claims against Rippling may proceed. Deel's most serious counterclaims, which allege Rippling pressured O'Brien into a false story and that he was a whistleblower, were sent to private arbitration.

Irish High Court (Judge Mark Sanfey): the court removed three Deel executives as defendants in Rippling's espionage case, struck one paragraph of Rippling's amended claim, and ordered Rippling to disclose its O'Brien termination agreement to Deel's lawyers under a confidentiality ring. The case continues against Deel Inc. Rippling dropped its claims against O'Brien in August 2025 after a co-operation agreement.

Deel says it sued Rippling in Delaware Superior Court in April and June 2025. It alleges a Rippling 'Competitive Intelligence Manager' used a fake company name to access Deel's platform 58 times, and alleges a broader pattern of anti-competitive conduct. Deel says it filed further federal counterclaims in April 2026. These are Deel's claims.

Sanctions exposure (allegation only): a Deel spokesperson said Rippling has faced accusations of violating Russian sanctions law. The Rippling complaint alleges sanctions issues at Deel. I opened no court ruling on either allegation.

Employee suits: a former engineering manager (Fu Zhou, March 2025) alleges she was fired after IVF medical leave; a February 2025 class action alleges unpaid 'off the clock' work. Both were moved to arbitration and their outcomes are unclear. Another former employee's suit, still ongoing, alleges he was fired after taking parental bonding leave. Rippling says it has never fired anyone for protected leave, never settled an FMLA claim, and never been found liable for one.

Runlayer sued Rippling on July 28, 2026 for trade-secret misappropriation and breach of contract. Rippling countersued for patent infringement on August 10, 2026. Both suits were dropped with no settlement and no money paid.

reputation.claim: Critical press: the Washington Free Beacon (a partisan outlet) reports a Glassdoor review calling Rippling's lack of paid leave for staff with under one year of service 'borderline barbaric'. It also reports that Rep. Lawler questioned New York's due diligence on Rippling's subsidies.
Critical press: TechCrunch reports that Rippling ran up millions in AI token costs within months, with one engineer spending $50K per month, before it brought in controls.
TechCrunch calls the Runlayer dispute 'a cautionary tale for founders'. Rippling tested Runlayer's MCP gateway for over a year, never became a customer, then released a competing gateway.
Fortune called the Deel spy case 'a major scandal rocking the HR world'. Rippling was the plaintiff.

red_flags.claim: Still burning cash: Conrad says Rippling is about two years from cash-flow positive, and R&D runs at 45–50% of revenue.

Deel litigation is expensive and runs in several courts. Deel's false-advertising claims partly survive, and its counterclaims that O'Brien was a whistleblower who was pressured are now in arbitration.
Several former-employee suits allege retaliation for leave and unpaid off-the-clock work. Some were moved to arbitration and their outcomes are unknown.
Russian-sanctions allegations have been raised against Rippling as part of the Deel dispute. They are unproven.
No new primary round since May 2025 ($16.8B), while revenue reportedly grew to about $1B. The valuation is now below Deel's ($17.3B) despite the reported growth.

output.verdict: The business looks strong: revenue reportedly passed $1B (a company claim, consistent with Sacra's estimates) and growth of about 78% YoY was still speeding up in April 2026. It has a broad, in-house-built HR, IT and finance suite, keeps launching products (Data Cloud, banking), a $16.8B last valuation and a seasoned leadership bench. Needs a closer look: cash burn (about two years to cash-flow positive, R&D at 45–50% of revenue), the multi-court Deel litigation including counterclaims in arbitration and unproven sanctions allegations, a pattern of former-employee labour suits pushed into arbitration, aggressive conduct toward smaller vendors (Runlayer), and unverified 2026 layoff and valuation data.
missing_fields: Company-verified current customer count (20,000+ is a May 2025 Sacra figure)
Exact Series F amount and full investor list for earlier rounds (Seed–Series E)
Lead investor for the Series G (not named in the company post)
Reported 2026 Series H ($425M at $17.5B) and Series I ($35B): each appears on only one aggregator, unverified and excluded
Secondary-market valuation mark (aggregator PremierAlts, about $16B as of Oct 2026): page not opened
Current 2026 headcount (only aggregator estimates, which conflict, from about 5,000 to 7,800)
2025–2026 layoffs: the Blind tracker reportedly lists about 600 cuts in Jan–Mar 2026, but the page returned 404, so unverified
Glassdoor rating and trend (page blocked, 403); search snippets suggested about 3.7/5 but this is not verified
Customer complaint patterns (BBB, G2, Trustpilot not checked)
Prasanna Sankar's current role or departure date
Executive departures in the last two years (none confirmed from a primary source)
Court dockets read directly: N.D. Cal. 3:25-cv-02576-CRB and Del. Super. N25C-04-239 (Justia returned 403)
Status of Deel's Delaware suit (a reported March 2026 dismissal is unverified)
Data breaches or regulator actions against Rippling (none found)
